title: Attainment of half the total variation by a single event
statement:
Let $\mu$ and $
u$ be probability measures on a measurable space $\Omega$, and let $\mu - 
u$ denote their signed measure difference. Then there exists a measurable set $S \subseteq \Omega$ at which
\[
\abs{(\mu - 
u)(S)} = 	frac{1}{2}\,\abs{\mu - 
u}(\Omega),
\]
where $\abs{\mu - 
u}$ is the total variation measure of $\mu - 
u$; that is, some event realizes exactly half the total variation of $\mu - 
u$ over the whole space.
hypotheses_covered: μ is a probability measure on Ω
ν is a probability measure on Ω
replaced:
There exists a measurable set $S \subseteq \Omega$ for which the bound is tight:
$|(\mu-\nu)(S)| = \tfrac{1}{2}\|\mu-\nu\|_{\mathrm{TV}}(\Omega)$.
